items.label: A
items.critique: Practical, mission-briefing plainness, with the spells handed over and a sneaking plan the player can act on. 'Good luck and good speed' and 'This may get very ugly, lad' sound like Westwood's mentor voice.

items.label: B
items.critique: The clipped fragments ('You'll know. And careful.') feel written to be terse rather than spoken. The reminder repeats the opening's instruction almost word for word, as if padding a template.

items.label: C
items.critique: Breathless exclamation with '!?', 'Damn!', a stakes-of-all-Nox line and a compass direction. This is Westwood's melodramatic, slightly clumsy urgency ('leaving rebuilding the village our smallest concern!').

items.label: D
items.critique: A mayor with comic petulance ('nettlesome urchins'), inconsistent capitals ('East', 'Urchins') and a reminder that gives no instruction at all. These are the loose edges of the shipped text.

items.label: E
items.critique: 'Forest beasts will heed its bite should they threaten' and 'the closer we get by air' are a writer's flourishes, not Nox's plain speech. The reminder piles up three stock hurry-ups.

items.label: F
items.critique: It ties the plot together too tidily ('with this as their prize, [Person] is most certainly behind it all'), and 'rest on laurels' and 'tested your mettle' are stock idioms. The opening sends the player both to recover the thing and to a person waiting, which muddies the task.

items.label: G
items.critique: The self-introduction is stiff ('The Master for the [Place]'), and 'convey' and 'the beast is housed' read oddly. The caps on 'YOU' imitate Westwood's emphasis but feel bolted on.

items.label: H
items.critique: Plain instructions in order: who to see, supplies and gold, the shop, the road over the bridges. The '--' and the 'I have nothing else to tell you' reminder are typical of the campaign's functional hand-offs.

items.label: I
items.critique: Short, proud, exclamatory introduction to a place, ending on a dry jab ('It weeds out the weak recruits'). It is economical, and its reminder is minimal.

items.label: J
items.critique: It reuses the mentor's drop-off beat ('as far as I can safely take you') with a generic 'You remain our only hope'. The journal over-specifies who the brother is, compared with Westwood's terse journal lines.

tells: New texts lean harder on the mentor's 'lad' and the stock hurry-up reminder ('Go! Get a move on', 'No more time for chit-chat') as if ticking boxes; Westwood's reminders vary more, and some give no instruction at all.
New texts reach for literary idioms and imagery ('heed its bite', 'rest on laurels', 'tested your mettle'), where Westwood's lines are plainer and more functional, or clumsy in a spoken way.
Westwood's texts have loose edges: inconsistent capitals, '!?', run-on exclamations, a mayor's pettiness. Generated texts are cleaner and tie plot threads together more neatly.
Journals that over-explain relationships or carry extra clauses read as generated; Westwood's journal lines are a short imperative naming one place or one person.
Westwood's openings list concrete logistics in order (supplies, gold, shop, road, spells, guards); generated openings spend more words on mood and stakes.
